column1: Repeated-measures (RM) design: definition & advantage
column2:
Same entities in all conditions / measured at several time points
Controls individual differences (e.g., tolerance, pain sensitivity)
Individual differences removed from error term
→ more power & sensitivity

column1: Composition of within-participant/within-group variance ($SS_W$): independent ANOVA vs. repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA
column2:
Independent: effect between groups; $SS_W$ = error + individual differences
RM: effect within participants; $SS_W$ = experimental effect + random error
RM: individual differences ($SS_B$) not part of error
F logic identical; only source of variance differs

column1: Sum-of-squares partitioning (one-way repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA)
column2:
$SS_T = SS_B + SS_W$
$SS_W = SS_M + SS_R$
$SS_B$: between-participants, individual differences → discarded (not error)
$SS_M$: model / effect of manipulation
$SS_R$: residual / error
$SS_M$, $SS_R$ entirely within-subject

column1: Sum-of-squares formulas (one-way repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA; $k$ conditions, $n$ subjects, $N=nk$)
column2:
$SS_T=\sum_i\sum_j (X_{ij}-\bar X_{grand})^2$ (shortcut: $\sum X^2 - N\bar X_{grand}^2$)
$SS_B = k\sum_i(\bar X_{i\cdot}-\bar X_{grand})^2$ (subject means)
$SS_W=\sum_i\sum_j (X_{ij}-\bar X_{i\cdot})^2=\sum_i s_i^2(k-1)$
$SS_M = n\sum_j(\bar X_{\cdot j}-\bar X_{grand})^2$ (condition means)
$SS_R = SS_W - SS_M$

column1: Degrees of freedom (df), mean squares (MS) & F-ratio (one-way repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA; $k$ conditions, $n$ subjects)
column2:
$df_T=N-1$; $df_B=n-1$; $df_W=n(k-1)$
$df_M=k-1$; $df_R=(k-1)(n-1)$ (not $N-k$)
$MS=SS/df$; only $MS_M$, $MS_R$ needed
$F=MS_M/MS_R$, $df=(k-1,(k-1)(n-1))$
Reject $H_0$ if $F_{obs}>F_{crit}(df_M,df_R,\alpha)$ → means differ across occasions

column1: Assumptions & checks (repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA)
column2:
Independence across subjects (dependence within subjects expected)
Normality per condition / of differences: Shapiro–Wilk
Sphericity: Mauchly
Homogeneity of variance only for between factor: Levene
No extreme outliers per condition

column1: Sphericity: definition & reason it is required (repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA)
column2:
Equal variances of differences between all pairs of conditions
Concerns difference scores, not condition variances
Standard ANOVA assumes independent conditions
RM scores related (same people) → independence violated → ordinary F inaccurate
Requires roughly equal dependence between any two conditions

column1: Checking sphericity by hand (3 conditions A, B, C)
column2:
Compute difference scores $A-B$, $A-C$, $B-C$ per subject
Variance of each difference
$Var(A-B)\approx Var(A-C)\approx Var(B-C)$ → sphericity (local) holds

column1: Mauchly's test: $H_0$, decision rule, caveats
column2:
$H_0$: sphericity holds
$p<.05$ → violated (significant = bad); $p>.05$ → not violated
Large samples: small deviations significant
Small samples: large violations undetected
Within-subjects factors only

column1: Number of factor levels for which sphericity is automatically met (repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA)
column2:
2 levels ($k=2$)
Only one difference score → nothing to compare
Sphericity relevant only for factors / interactions with > 2 levels

column1: Consequences of sphericity violation (repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA)
column2:
F-ratio inaccurate
Inflated Type I error rate
Loss of power
Post hoc tests behave unpredictably

column1: Sphericity correction: mechanism & range of epsilon ($\hat\varepsilon$)
column2:
Estimate $\hat\varepsilon$; multiply both df ($df_M$, $df_R$) by it
F unchanged; p recomputed with corrected df
$\varepsilon_{max}=1$: perfect sphericity
Lower bound $\varepsilon_{min}=1/(k-1)$ (e.g., $k=3$: 0.5), most conservative

column1: Greenhouse–Geisser (GG) vs. Huynh–Feldt (HF): conservativeness & selection rule (sphericity correction)
column2:
GG (1959): more conservative
HF (1976): less conservative (liberal)
$\hat\varepsilon<0.75$ → GG
$\hat\varepsilon>0.75$ → HF
Alternative: average both

column1: Post hoc test choice depending on sphericity (repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA)
column2:
Sphericity violated → Bonferroni
Sphericity not violated → Tukey

column1: Alternatives to repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA avoiding the sphericity assumption
column2:
MANOVA (multivariate ANOVA)-based test statistics: no sphericity assumed
Multilevel / mixed-effects models: multiple observations per participant; explicitly model covariance structure; pairwise comparison of effects
Mixed-effects models = robust choice when in doubt

column1: Two-way (factorial) repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA: design, tested effects, SS partitioning, error terms
column2:
≥ 2 within-subject factors; each participant does every combination (2×2 → 4 cells)
Tests main effect A, main effect B, A×B interaction
$SS_T=SS_{Between}+SS_{Within}$; $SS_{Within}=SS_A+SS_B+SS_{A\times B}+SS_{Error}$
Each effect has its own error term
Mauchly for every factor / interaction with > 2 levels; GG/HF if violated

column1: Mixed-design ANOVA: definition & assumption checks
column2:
≥ 1 within factor (e.g., time) + ≥ 1 between factor (different people per group)
Within factor (> 2 levels): sphericity, Mauchly
Between factor: homogeneity of variance, Levene

column1: Degrees of freedom (df) of each effect & error term (mixed-design ANOVA; $g$ groups, $k$ within levels, $n$ participants)
column2:
Between effect: $g-1$; between error: $n-g$
Within effect: $k-1$
Interaction: $(g-1)(k-1)$
Within error: $(k-1)(n-g)$
e.g., $F(1,8)$ with 2 groups → $n=10$

column1: Required data format for repeated-measures (RM) ANOVA in Pingouin (Python)
column2:
Long format
One row per participant per condition
Columns: participant ID | condition (factor) | DV
Trial-level data → aggregate (mean per participant × condition)

column1: Reporting checklist (repeated-measures (RM) / mixed ANOVA)
column2:
F, df, p for every main effect & interaction
Sphericity violated → corrected df & p
Effect size: partial $\eta^2=SS_{effect}/(SS_{effect}+SS_{error})$
Significant effects → corrected post hoc tests, interaction plots
Non-significant interaction → main effects directly; significant → main effects with caution
